conflicts.outcome: The ruling's validation and persistence override wins: the real checks (country in list, saved country still listed, region code length, internal reference length, valid radio value) stay, and a refused save stores nothing. prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-059, -p2-061 and -p2-063 are not overruled: they still back the country being optional, the absence of a format rule and trimming, which stand.

conflicts.about: Whether the ruling's real-constraint override covers accessibility and no-JavaScript use, where the prototype's hand-built markup falls short.

positions.says: Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service) overrides the prototype.
The ruling does not say whether a constrained service keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as it can.
The origin page keeps its title in an error state, with no 'Error: ' prefix.
The country search box has no label; the 'Country of origin' heading is not associated with it.
The region code input is not linked to its hint or error.
The country search is a custom component outside the GOV.UK toolbox.
In an error state the browser title is prefixed 'Error: '.
Without JavaScript the country question is a plain labelled GOV.UK select.

conflicts.outcome: Open: the ruling lists persistence, validation, authentication and cross-service behaviour, and its list can be read as examples or as complete; the two readings build different markup.
conflicts.question: Does the ruling's real-constraint override cover accessibility and no-JavaScript use, so the real pages keep their accessible build where the prototype's markup falls short?
conflicts.default: Yes: keep the 'Error: ' title prefix, a real 'Country of origin' label on an accessible-autocomplete over a native select that works without JavaScript, and the region code input linked to its hint and error with the error style; within that build, match the prototype's visible copy, placeholder, search icon and search behaviour.

conflicts.about: How the notification type question maps onto the real services, when only the live-animals journey is in this programme.

positions.says: A general start goes to the notification type question.
Every type, including plants for planting, potatoes and wood products, continues to the live-animals origin page.
A plants-for-planting draft still gets a GBN-AG reference.
Plants for planting runs the same origin and commodity pages as live animals, and nothing can be picked.
Starting a notification from the dashboard lands straight on the live-animals origin page.
Which repos change is worked out from the evidence.

conflicts.outcome: Open: the design cannot be met as written for the four non-live-animals types, which no service in this programme can take, and the evidence does not fix which service hosts the question.
conflicts.question: Which service hosts the notification type question, and what do Germinal products, Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) and Wood products do when the live-animals journey is the only one this programme builds?
conflicts.default: The INS front door hosts the type question, reached from its all-types dashboard's start link (which today goes straight into the animals frontend), with DR2.1's title, caption, Back link and Continue button. Live animals continues to the animals frontend's existing start, which creates the GBN-AG draft and lands on origin, and origin's Back link returns to the type question. Plants for planting continues to the start of the high-risk plants journey in trade-imports-plants-frontend. Germinal products, Potatoes (seed and ware) and Wood products are left off the list until a service can take them. The animals frontend's own live-animals dashboard acts as the category dashboard and its start skips the question. Re-selecting a type on return applies only where the notification already exists.

conflicts.about: Whether the region code prefix follows the country live in the browser.

positions.says: DR1 deferred the live prefix, to be decided with design and, if required, built with the country control.
The no-JavaScript prefix stays server-side as shipped until decided.
The prefix map is sent to the page so the prefix follows the picked country.
Picking France fills the prefix with FR with no submission.
Today the prefix appears only after the page is re-rendered.

conflicts.outcome: DR1's deferral, the highest-ranked position, said to decide with design and build the live prefix with the country control if design requires it; Design Release 2.1 is that design decision and requires it. So the live prefix is built as a progressive enhancement, with an empty prefix slot before a country is chosen, and without JavaScript the server-side prefix stays as DR1 shipped it.

conflicts.about: The country control's visible copy and behaviour: hint, placeholder, opening on focus, drop-down arrow, match highlighting and announcements.

positions.says: The prototype wins by default over what the real services do today.
The country search has no hint.
The search box has the placeholder 'Search for a country' and a search button.
Typing opens matching results with the typed letters in bold.
The field has the hint 'Start typing to search for a country.'
The type-ahead offers the whole list on focus.
The box shows a drop-down arrow.
Results show plain names with no highlighting.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype outranks the real frontend and no DR1 judgement or real constraint touches these differences, so the country control takes the prototype's copy and behaviour (requirements 015 to 020). Today's claims are not overruled: they are the evidence of what each change replaces.

conflicts.about: The region of origin code question's hint, the code box's character cap and whether No clears a saved code.

positions.says: The prototype wins by default over what the real services do today.
The hint is 'Check the health certificate for a region of origin code. You can add the code later if you do not have the certificate now.'
The code input accepts at most 5 characters.
Answering No clears any saved region code.
The hint is 'If a region of origin code is required it will be shown on your health certificate.'
A code saved under Yes is kept when the answer changes to No.
The code box has no maxlength.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype outranks the real frontend and no DR1 judgement or real constraint touches these differences: the hint changes, the box caps typing at 5 characters (the server check stays, under c-start-and-origin-005), and No clears the saved code. Today's claims stay cited as the evidence of what changes.

conflicts.about: The internal reference hint and the origin page's Back link.

positions.says: The prototype wins by default over what the real services do today.
The internal reference hint ends at 'or leave blank.'
The Back link goes to the type question, the category dashboard or the template it came from.
The hint adds 'It can be up to 58 characters.'
The Back link goes to the dashboard until answers are saved, then to the overview.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype outranks the real frontend: the hint drops the 58-character sentence (the limit itself is a real validation constraint and stays enforced with its error, which names it), and the Back link follows where the user came from. Today's claims stay cited as the evidence of what changes.
